rooms.1402: The stair is a spiral groove worn into the heartwood of a tree so vast that its trunk seems more a tower than a plant. Lanterns of pale glass sit in niches along the curve, and the wood glows amber where their light touches it. The woven silver gate that once closed the foot of the stair now stands open, and the way down leads back to the roots of the great tree beside the trade road. Above, the steps climb on into the green dark.
rooms.1403: Here the stair narrows, and the curve of the trunk presses close on one hand, its bark rubbed smooth by countless soft-soled feet. Slits in the wood let in thin green light and the hush of leaves, and now and then a breath of wind carries a sweet, resinous smell. Carved vines twine up the inner wall, each leaf cut so finely that it seems to tremble. The steps run down toward the lower flights and up toward a ceiling of pale, gleaming timber.
rooms.1404: The stair ends beneath the underside of a great platform, a ceiling of interwoven boughs grown flat and tight as planking. Light filters down through the seams in slivers of gold, and the whole structure creaks softly, like a ship at anchor. A rope-wrapped banister of braided bark follows the steps, which climb to a square opening where the open air waits. Below, the flights wind away down the trunk.
rooms.1421: You step out onto the common platform at its corner, where a rail of living branches curves around the edge and the ground lies unimaginably far below. The planks are pale, smooth and warm underfoot, laid so tightly that no leaf-shadow slips between them. Lanterns hang from the rail on silver chains, swaying a little in the breeze. The platform stretches on east along the rail and south along the edge, while the stairs lead down into the trunk.
rooms.1422: A broad branch meets the platform's edge here, and the rail breaks to let it through. The planks are inlaid with a pattern of silver leaves that catch the lantern light as you walk. Wind-chimes of thin glass tinkle among the boughs overhead, and the leaves hiss like a distant sea. The platform spreads out east and west along its edge and south toward its middle, while the branch called Moredhel climbs away north.
rooms.1420: Moredhel Branch begins here as a broad living road, its upper surface flattened and strewn with fine moss. Railings of woven twigs rise on both sides, and between them the branch runs north into a hush of denser leaves. Back to the south the common platform is a bright open space, full of the soft clink of lanterns. Small blue flowers grow in the crooks where the lesser twigs leave the bough.
rooms.1418: Here the branch widens into a little crossing, with a door cut into the bark on either hand. The door east is heavy and banded with bronze, its panels scored by practice blades, while the door west is narrow, dark and oddly silent on its hinges. The planking is deep green and soft with moss, and ferns hang from the boughs above. The branch runs on north toward the clerics and mages, and south back to the platform.
rooms.1415: The branch ends in a small round court, its floor a single great knot of polished wood. A doorway wreathed in white blossoms leads east to the Clerics Guild, and a door carved with stars and crescents opens west into the Mages Guild. Light from a hanging globe pools over the knot, and the whole court smells of incense and crushed leaves. The branch you came by runs back south.
rooms.1416: This chapel was grown rather than built, its walls curving up into a vaulted ceiling of living wood hung with strands of glowing moss. At its heart a basin of clear water rests on a pedestal of white stone, ringed with offerings of blossoms and folded leaves. Low benches of pale birch face it, and soft songs seem to hang in the air even when the room is quiet. The only way out is the door west to the end of the branch.
rooms.1414: Shelves spiral up the curve of the walls, crowded with scrolls, glass spheres and little bound books whose covers shift colour in the light. A table of grey ash-wood bears a half-finished diagram in silver wire, and motes of pale light drift lazily near the ceiling. The air tingles faintly and smells of cedar and lightning. The one way out is the arched door east, which opens to the end of the branch.
rooms.1419: A long hall of living wood, its floor sanded smooth for sparring and its walls hung with targets of woven reed. Racks along the sides hold wooden practice swords, long bows and quarterstaffs worn pale by use. Beams of green light fall through high windows, and the boards bear the scuffs of countless footwork drills. The only door lies west, back onto the branch.
rooms.1417: A low, close room where the lamps are shuttered to a single slit and the corners are deep with shadow. A table scattered with lock-picks, coils of fine cord and little velvet pouches sits beneath a hanging net of dry leaves that rustles at the slightest breath. The floorboards have been laid to creak in a pattern, and a careful foot learns to step around the loud ones. The door east is the only way out, onto the branch.
rooms.1423: The corner of the platform curves to a point here, where the rail swells into a fat living post carved with a ring of dancing figures. Beyond the rail the crowns of other great trees stretch away like a green ocean under the sky. The planks run west along the edge and south along the rail, and a stair opens in the floor, leading down into the trunk. Gold-tinted lanterns hang from the post on twisted cords.
rooms.1433: The platform's rim runs close by here, hung with lanterns shaped like seed-pods that shine soft gold. A branch leaves the platform east as a wide walkway, its rail woven into a trellis of climbing white roses. The planking is worn into pale hollows where many feet have passed, and a gentle breeze brings the smell of baking and woodsmoke. The platform carries on north and south along the rail, and west toward its middle.
rooms.1434: Glamredhel Branch begins its long curve here, springing from the platform as a boughway broad enough for a wagon. Small lamps hang from hooks along its rail, and the planks give faintly underfoot, with the springy feel of a ship's deck. Names of old craftsmen run along the rail in swirling script. The walkway leads on east toward the shops, and back west to the open platform.
rooms.1435: The branch is busiest here, where doors open on both sides under signs of carved leaf and steel. The sign over the north door shows a bow crossed with a blade, and the sign over the south door a mail shirt hung on a bough. Overhead the boughs lace together into a canopy that scatters green-gold light across the planks, and bright ribbons tied to the rail flutter in the wind. West the walkway heads back to the platform, and east it winds on.
rooms.1426: Bows of yew, ash and horn hang from the curved walls in tidy ranks, their strings coiled beside them like sleeping snakes. Glass cases hold daggers with leaf-shaped blades, and on a bench in the corner lies a half-strung longbow beside a pot of wax. The wooden floor is bare and swept, and the smell is of oil and cut timber. The door south opens onto the branch.
rooms.1436: The branch ends in a rounded knob, a broad little balcony whose rail looks out over a sea of leaves. A door under a carved sprig of healing herbs opens north, and a wide round door with a hanging lantern opens south. Pots of lavender and mint stand along the rail, scenting the air. Back west the walkway returns toward the shops.
rooms.1427: A long bright room where cots of woven willow stand in a line beneath windows hung with white linen. Bunches of drying herbs sway from the beams, and on a low table sit jars of salve, rolled bandages and a bowl of steaming water. The air is clean and sweet with yarrow and mint. The door south leads out to the balcony at the end of the branch.
rooms.1440: The inn's common room is warm and low, with a hearth of smooth river stones where a small fire burns and a kettle sings. Chairs of bent wood sit about tables carved with trailing ivy, and lanterns hang from the beams in clusters. Rows of keys hang on pegs behind the counter, each tagged with a painted leaf, and the smell of spiced cider fills the air. The door north opens onto the end of the branch.
rooms.1439: Suits of leather and fine scale mail stand on wooden frames shaped like slender figures, each polished until it gleams. Helms and bracers lie on shelves, laid out on cloth of green velvet, and a bench holds awls, rivets and a half-stitched greave. Light from a lantern glints along rows of buckles on the wall. The door north leads out to the branch.
rooms.1443: The platform ends in another corner here, its rail curved to meet itself around a small carved basin of rainwater. A pair of fruit trees in tubs of black earth lean over the planks, scattering petals across the pale wood. A stair in the floor leads down into the great trunk, and the platform runs north along the rail and west along the edge. Lanterns shaped like seed-pods hang from the corner posts.
rooms.1442: The platform narrows here where Eledhel Branch leaves it, a thick bough of dark, glossy bark that runs away south toward the royal halls. Great planters of fern and white lilies stand at the mouth of the bough, and the rail is carved with leaping hounds. The planks are scrubbed so clean that they seem to hold the light. The platform opens north toward its middle, and east and west along its edge.
rooms.1432: At the heart of the platform the planks are laid in a great spiral of pale and dark wood, winding in to a small round inlay of silver at the centre. Overhead the boughs part to frame a disc of sky, and the sun falls through in a slow bright circle. Benches shaped from single roots curve around the rim of the spiral. Lantern-lit walkways lead away on all four sides, north, east, south and west.
rooms.1431: Here the platform's planking is stained to a deep honey colour and rubbed bright by many hands. Clusters of paper lanterns hang from a cord strung between two posts, and a faint smell of bread drifts in along the walkway heading west. A shallow carved gutter runs along the rail, carrying rainwater out to the edge. The platform continues north and south, while east it opens toward its middle.
rooms.1441: In this corner a low wall of woven branches curves around a bed of ferns and moonflowers grown in a trough of earth. The rail beyond is carved with wading birds, and under the lanterns the planks are scattered with dew-bright petals. A stairway sunk into the floor spirals down inside the trunk. The platform runs north along its rail and east along its edge.
rooms.1410: The stair rises into a tight space beneath the platform, its ceiling a thick weave of branches that creaks and shifts with the breeze. A lantern of green glass hangs from a hook, tinting the wood and the steps to the colour of pond water. Each tread has been worn into a shallow dish by long use. Above, a square opening shows the bright platform, and below, the flights wind down the trunk.
rooms.1409: The stair coils tightly round the heart of the tree here, its steps carved from a single spiral ridge of living wood. Knots in the bark have been polished into little round windows, through which glimpses of sunlit leaves show. A thin cord of braided vine serves as a handrail. The smell is of resin and warm sap, and the only sound is the soft creak of the great tree settling in the wind.
rooms.1408: The lowest flight of the stair curls down to the foot of the tree, where the door of living bark that once barred it now stands wide, its edges folded back like petals. Cool air and the scent of earth and roots rise from the opening. Rings are carved into the wall to mark the tree's old years, each rimmed with a whisper of silver paint. The steps lead up into the lantern-lit heights and down to the roots.
rooms.1430: The western branch springs from the platform here, a long arm of pale wood curving away under a trellis of climbing honeysuckle. Wind-bells of bone and silver hang along it, and each breath of air sets them murmuring. The planks are scrubbed and sprinkled with seed-husks, the leavings of some bird-feeding. Back east the broad platform opens out, and westward the branch goes on toward the market doors.
rooms.1429: Two doors face each other across the walkway, one under a sign of a bundled sheaf and the other beneath a painted loaf. The branch here is wide and flat, its rail festooned with ivy and strings of dried apples. Warm bread smells drift out from the south, mixed with the sharper tang of rope and tar from the north. The branch runs west toward more doors, and east to the platform.
rooms.1425: Shelves climb to the ceiling, crowded with coils of rope, lanterns, waterskins, wooden bowls and bundles of arrows tied with ribbon. A ladder of woven cord leans against one wall, and sacks of dried fruit slump in a corner. The room smells of tar, wax and cedar, and a brass bell hangs on a spring over the counter. The door south leads back to the branch.
rooms.1438: A great clay oven fills one wall, glowing orange through its iron door and warming the whole room. Trays of honey cakes, seed loaves and braided rolls cool on racks of pale wood. The floor is dusted with flour, and a long table scarred by years of kneading stands in the middle. The smell is wonderful, sweet with honey and nutty with toasted grain. The door north returns to the branch.
rooms.1428: The branch ends at a round platform of its own, circled by a rail of silvery twigs and shaded by a leaning bough thick with glossy leaves. A door of blue-tinted wood marked with a spiral of stars opens north, and a plain brown door hung with a carved antler opens south. Small lights drift in the foliage like fireflies, though no insects hover there. The way east leads back along the branch.
rooms.1424: Glass bottles of every hue fill the shelves, each holding a drifting mist or a slow, spinning spark. Wands lie in a velvet-lined tray, and a cloud of tiny lights shifts about the ceiling like a flock of silent birds. The counter is a slab of polished amber wood engraved with runes of silver. The air hums faintly and smells of mint and thunder. A door south opens to the branch.
rooms.1437: Smoked haunches hang from hooks in the rafters, turning slowly in the warm draught, and strings of dried sausage swing beside them. A heavy chopping block, scored deep by cleavers, stands at the room's heart, and jars of salt and juniper line the shelves. The air is thick with woodsmoke and herbs. A door north opens onto the end of the branch.
rooms.1444: Eledhel Branch is the royal road, a thick and glossy bough broad enough for six to walk abreast. Its planks are laid in a pattern of dark and pale wood, and its railings are carved with the leaves of the oak, the beech and the elm. Lanterns of green glass hang at regular intervals, swaying gently. The platform lies close behind to the north, and the branch runs on south toward the royal halls.
rooms.1445: The bough stretches long and straight here, its surface sanded smooth and sprinkled with the tiny petals of some night-blooming vine. Silken banners the colour of new leaves hang from the rail, each stitched with a silver tree. Through the gaps beneath the rail, sunlight dapples the distant ground far below. The branch runs north toward the platform and south onward.
rooms.1447: A crossing of the branch, where doors of thick dark wood face each other beneath lintels carved with crossed spears. Slender lamps burn at each door, never guttering despite the wind. The planks are scuffed by the tread of boots, and a polished horn hangs on a hook beside the east door. Beyond the rail the leaves rustle like a crowd. The branch runs north and south, with a guard room on either side.
rooms.1448: A plain, tidy room where spears and long swords stand in racks along the curved wall. A table of grey wood holds a map of the city's branches drawn on stretched bark, weighted at its corners with smooth pebbles. Narrow windows let in the green light and the sound of leaves. Bunks of woven cord are tucked against the far wall. The door west opens onto the branch.
rooms.1450: Doors of finely grained pale wood stand on either side of the branch, each marked by a brass plate inscribed in elegant script. The planks are brushed clean and polished until they gleam, and a faint sweet smell of beeswax lingers. Ferns in hanging baskets drip dew from the rail. The branch leads north toward the platform and south on toward the royal waiting hall.
rooms.1451: A quiet study lit by a lamp with a shade of green glass. Maps and scrolls lie across a broad desk of dark burr-wood, and pigeonholes along one wall are stuffed with sealed letters. The chair is high-backed and deep, cushioned in grey wool. Everything is orderly, from the quills to the ink-stones. The door west leads back to the branch.
rooms.1453: The branch widens before a great carved archway, and the planks are inlaid with a long band of silver leaves pointing the way. Guard rooms stand to either side behind sturdy doors, east and west, and the rail is ornamented with flowing knots of woven brass. The air is cool and still, with the scent of beeswax and bark. South, the archway opens into the waiting area of the throne room, and the branch runs back north.
rooms.1454: A narrow room smelling of oil and leather, where the walls are hung with quivers, bucklers and scabbards on pegs. A long bench runs beneath the window, and a rack of whetstones sits beside a lamp. A board scratched with the names of old watches hangs by the door. The floor shows a path worn by many pacing boots. The door west returns to the branch.
rooms.1456: A grand hall of living wood, its ceiling a vault of woven boughs hung with glowing globes. Tall benches of white ash face a pair of towering doors set with silver leaves, and a carpet of deep moss green runs between them. The walls curve outward into two quiet wings, one reached east and one west. North the archway returns to the branch outside, and the great doors south lead to the throne room.
rooms.1457: A small alcove off the waiting hall, with cushioned window-seats overlooking the shimmering sea of leaves. A low table holds a bowl of fruit and a pitcher of cool water. Tapestries of green and silver thread, showing a hunt beneath a pale moon, cover the wall. It is a place for waiting, and for thinking over what one means to say. The way back is west into the main waiting area.
rooms.1458: The throne room is a vast chamber formed by living boughs grown into pillars and arches, its ceiling lost in a haze of glimmering leaves. At the far end stands a high seat of silver-grey wood, its back a spray of carved branches twined with stars. A long carpet of deep green runs between rows of slender columns, each carved with the history of a reign. Light of no visible source gilds everything. The doors north lead back to the waiting hall, and a small door south is closed behind the throne.
rooms.1459: A narrow stair, hidden behind the throne room, spirals down inside the heart of the tree. The walls are close and warm, and the steps are carved with tiny leaf patterns that grip the foot. A single lantern hangs from a hook, its glow steady and pale. The door north leads back to the throne room, while the stair continues down toward the lower branch.
rooms.1466: The inner corridor opens here into a wider gallery of living wood, its floor sloping gently with the grain of the tree. Roots as thick as pillars arch overhead, and lanterns of dim amber hang in the hollows between them. The air is cool and smells of earth and sap. A stair rises behind you to the private stairway, and the gallery runs on north and south.
rooms.1464: A crossroads of galleries cut in the heartwood, where low arches open on every side. The floor is worn smooth with the tread of countless boots, and the walls are hung with the old banners of the watch, faded green and silver. A single iron brazier burns at the junction, its smoke drawn up into some hidden flue. The archway north leads to barracks, the arches east and west to more of the same, and the gallery runs back south.
rooms.1462: Rows of narrow bunks are built into the curving walls, each with a folded green blanket and a small shelf for a few treasured things. A weapon rack stands at the end of every row, and a long table in the centre is scarred by the marks of dice and blades. The ceiling beams are blackened with lamp smoke. A narrow door north leads on to the laboratory, and the arch south opens to the gallery.
rooms.1461: Long benches of dark wood hold alembics, retorts and racks of glass vials, all joined by a tangle of silver tubing. Bundles of strange roots and pale mushrooms hang drying from the rafters, and a faint green fume curls from a bubbling flask. Charts of runes and poisons crowd the walls, some scorched at the edges. A heavy passage north leads on toward the adamantium gates of a drow city, while an arch south returns to the barracks.
rooms.1465: A smaller barracks chamber, its low ceiling braced with ribs of living wood. Hammocks of cord hang in two tiers, and each post has hooks for a cloak, a quiver and a lantern. A small shrine of carved leaves stands in one corner, with a sprig of fresh greenery laid before it. The air smells of leather and boiled tea. The only way out is the arch west into the lower branch.
rooms.1463: Here the barracks are given over to training: grain-filled bags hang from the beams, and wooden dummies stand scarred by sword strokes. Long benches line the wall, and above them hang rows of dull practice blades. A water barrel with a ladle sits in a corner beside a stack of towels. The low hum of the tree itself fills the room. The arch east opens to the lower branch.
rooms.1467: Another crossing of the lower gallery, its walls carved with a long frieze of marching elves beneath streaming banners. A medallion of green tile, showing a tree in full leaf, is set into the floor to mark the junction. Arches open east, south and west, and the gallery runs back north toward the stair. A draught carries the smell of oil and metal.
rooms.1471: A quiet chamber where off-duty watchers sleep, with rows of cots covered in grey wool and a rack for boots by the arch. A shuttered lantern hangs from the central beam, throwing a dim glow across a chest of spare cloaks. Someone has carved a tally of days into one post. The air is warm and stale, and smells faintly of pipe-leaf. The arch west leads to the lower branch.
rooms.1468: A sturdy room near the treasury, with thick roots grown into a rack of spears along each wall. A heavy table holds a ledger sealed with a brass clasp and a ring of keys on a hook. The door in the south wall is bound in silver and kept shut, with a spyhole carved in its centre. The air is tense and watchful. An opening north leads back to the lower branch.
rooms.1469: A round vault grown inside the tree's heart, its walls lined with shelves and chests of dark wood bound with silver. Trays of cut gems glitter beside niches of old crowns resting on cushions of faded velvet. A runic ward on the lintel flickers faintly. The air is dry and still, and the only sound is the slow settling of the tree. The door north leads back to the barracks.
rooms.1470: This barracks smells of sharpened steel and wax. Racks of long bows and tall shields stand along the wall, and a worktable bears whetstones, bowstring wax and a dish of arrowheads. The beams are carved with a pattern of hawks. A narrow window of bark-thin glass shows nothing but a deep green dusk. Through the arch east lies the lower branch.
rooms.1455: A quiet alcove off the waiting hall, cooler than its twin and hung with curtains of pale silk. A reading desk bears a thick volume of elven genealogies, and a vase of white lilies scents the air. The window looks out on the swaying canopy, where the light flickers between the leaves. A faint sound of lute music drifts in from somewhere. The way out is east to the main hall.
rooms.1452: A room of sturdy practicality: a table of scrubbed oak, a rack of halberds, and a chest bound with a lock of grey iron. A map of the branches hangs on the wall, pricked with pins of coloured thread. Gentle light falls from a round window of leaded glass. The boards bear a faint path along the wall where long patrols have turned. A door east opens onto the branch.
rooms.1449: A cosy, book-cluttered office with deep shelves, a small writing desk and a pair of armchairs facing a window of coloured glass. Rolled maps lean in a basket, and a lamp throws golden light across a stack of petitions bound with ribbon. A warm smell of old paper hangs in the air. A faded tapestry shows the founding of the city. The door east returns to the branch.
rooms.1446: A watch-room with a view, its single window opening onto the branch and the green leaf-sea beyond. A table bears a game of carved stones, left in mid-play, and an hourglass of silver and glass. Spears are racked beside the door, and a cloak hangs on a peg. The floor is polished by years of patient waiting. The door east is the way out to the branch.
rooms.1413: The stair ends beneath a canopy of woven boughs, where bars of light fall through the cracks in the ceiling in glowing stripes. A handrail of carved ivy runs beside the steps, worn smooth by many palms. Above, an opening leads up to the platform, and below, the stair winds down around the trunk. A cool draught slips up from the depths.
rooms.1412: Midway down the trunk the stair broadens into a landing, where an alcove in the wall holds a bench shaped from a single root. A small window in the bark looks out over the swaying crowns of lesser trees far below. Moss grows in a soft green carpet on the steps. The air is cool and full of the scent of green things. The flights lead up to the platform and down toward the trunk's foot.
rooms.1411: The lowest steps of this stair were once tangled with ivy and wild rose, but a path has been cut through, and the curtain is now drawn aside. Thorny stems still cling to the wall, laced with small pink blossoms. Fallen petals lie thick on the steps, and the smell is sweet and slightly wild. Light from below shows the cleft in the trunk where the stair meets the world. The flights climb up into the tree and go down to the cleft at its foot.
rooms.1407: A short flight of steps runs up to a trapdoor of silver-barked wood set into the platform's underside. The air here is brighter and moves with the wind, and the creak of the boughs is louder than lower down. Strands of ivy trail through gaps in the planks overhead. The stair winds down around the trunk, its handrail carved with a running pattern of leaves.
rooms.1406: A turn of the stair, where the wall of the trunk bulges out into a great burl, polished by the touch of many hands to the colour of dark honey. A lantern in a bracket gleams on it. Pale lichens speckle the opposite wall like scattered coins. A slow tapping echoes somewhere inside the wood. The steps go up toward the platform and down toward the roots.
rooms.1405: The lowest flight of the stair ends at a landing high above the roots, and a ladder of silver rope has been let down from it to the ground. Where it once hung drawn up, it now dangles free, its rungs swaying lightly. Great loops of root arch beneath, forming a green-lit hall between earth and trunk. Cool air rises from below, smelling of leaf-mould. The steps climb up into the tree, and the ladder leads down.

1423.description: The living post is carved all round with slender dancers, hand in hand, each wearing a crown of leaves. Their faces are worn faint by the touch of passing palms.

1432.description: The silver inlay is set flush with the planks, a small tree of fine wire with seven branches. Its roots spread out in the spiral of the floor, as if the whole platform grew from it.

1458.description: The seat is grown rather than carved, its arms two boughs that curve inward and its back a fan of branches studded with tiny silver stars. It is empty, yet it seems to be waiting.

1469.description: The ward is a line of silver runes inlaid in the lintel. They pulse faintly, in the slow rhythm of a sleeping heart.

1405.description: The ladder is made of braided silver cord, light as a spider's thread yet strong, with rungs of pale wood. Its upper end is tied off to a ring in the landing.

creatures.long_desc: A slender elf in a cloak of leaf-green strolls along the boughs, humming softly.
creatures.description: She is tall and fine-boned, with swept ears and eyes the colour of new leaves. Her cloak is clasped with a small silver brooch, and she walks with the unhurried grace of one who has never feared a fall.

creatures.long_desc: An elven merchant waits behind a counter, arranging wares with careful fingers.
creatures.description: He has a quick, courteous smile and ink-stained fingers. A ring of tiny keys hangs at his belt, and his eyes miss nothing that passes his door.

creatures.long_desc: An elven guard in green and silver stands watch, one hand resting on a slim sword.
creatures.description: The guard wears a shirt of fine linked mail beneath a leaf-green surcoat. His face is calm and watchful, and he carries himself like one who has stood many long watches in the high branches.

creatures.long_desc: An elven guildmaster stands here with folded arms, ready to teach those who ask.
creatures.description: Ageless and unhurried, the guildmaster studies each visitor with a long, measuring look. Years of training others have given the elf a quiet, patient authority.

creatures.long_desc: An elven archmage sits among drifting motes of light, turning a glass sphere in her hands.
creatures.description: Her robes are the grey of morning mist, stitched along the hems with silver runes that shimmer when she moves. Her eyes are deep and old, and small sparks gather at her fingertips when she is thinking.

creatures.long_desc: An elven warmaster paces the sparring floor, watching every stroke with a critical eye.
creatures.description: Lean and scarred, the warmaster moves with the economy of a blade being drawn. Her hair is bound in a long braid, and a worn sword hangs at her hip as though it were part of her.

creatures.long_desc: The captain of the guard stands tall in silver-trimmed mail, surveying her watch.
creatures.description: Captain Elrienna is tall even for an elf, with grey eyes and a long scar along one cheek. Her silver-trimmed mail is polished bright, and her leaf-bladed sword never seems far from her hand.

items.room_desc: A leaf-green elven cloak lies here.
items.description: Woven of fine grey-green wool, the cloak shifts colour like leaves in the wind. It is light as a sigh and warm as a hearth.

items.room_desc: A silver leaf brooch lies here.
items.description: A tiny leaf of silver, veined with exquisite lines, made to clasp a cloak. Such work fetches a good price from any collector.

items.room_desc: A shirt of fine elven mail lies here.
items.description: Thousands of tiny rings, each no bigger than a lentil, make up this supple shirt. It weighs almost nothing yet turns a blade like a plate.

items.room_desc: A thin silver circlet lies here.
items.description: A narrow band of silver, set at the brow with a single pale stone. It hums faintly and sharpens the thoughts of whoever wears it.

items.room_desc: A long leaf-bladed sword lies here.
items.description: The blade is broad at the middle and tapers to a needle point, etched with a pattern of veins. Its grip is wound with green silk, and it feels perfectly balanced.
